stories.title: Apec summit live: Xi and Putin start talks; Rubio says Trump serious about meeting Kim Jong-un
stories.summary: Summit in Chinese tech hub Shenzhen set to include highly anticipated meeting between Xi, Trump and Putin Shenzhen takes centre stage as Xi sends ‘Chinamaxxing’ message at Apec summit What is Apec? Explained in 30 seconds Yalta became a byword for betrayal. Will Trump, Xi and Putin enact another carve-up? That is the question the Guardian’s diplomatic correspondent Patrick Wintour seeks to address in his piece about the expected, Putin, Trump and Xi, meeting at Apec on Thursday. It is a truism in diplomacy that if you are not around the table, the risk is that you, or your values, are on the menu and about to be carved up. Many excluded from the summit in Shenzhen, principally Ukraine but also eastern Europe and Baltic countries, Taiwan and even Iran, have reason to be nervous that their sponsors might abandon them in a complex geopolitical trade-off that Putin envisions, and Trump seems to endorse. Continue reading...

stories.title: £10m ‘once-in-a-generation’ study to explore effects of children’s social media ban
stories.summary: Research to look at whether ban can make meaningful change in mental health and wellbeing for under-16s Countries around the world are considering social media bans for children, but whether this would work in practice has been hotly debated. Now researchers are seeking answers through a major scientific study led by Wellcome, which will be the first of its kind. Ten research projects will explore topics ranging from children’s mental health to their sleep and physical activity, comparing factors before and after the social media ban for children under 16 is introduced in the UK in spring 2027. stories.title: ‘Zero’ evidence that recent cascade of tech outages are linked, says Rubio
stories.summary: The US secretary of state was speaking after Microsoft, major banks, and the National Security Agency were all affected by technical failures in recent days US secretary of state Marco Rubio has sought to assure Americans that there’s “zero” information that the cascade of service outages – which have grounded flights, cut off work access, limited bank access and disrupted classified communications – are related to each other or to a malign actor.
